title: Managing Community Conversations on Sensitive Race and Religion Topics and Addressing Tensions due to Racial Insensitivities
what_it_is: Managing Community Conversations on Sensitive Race and Religion Topics and Addressing Tensions due to Racial Insensitivities

sections.label: Civic engagement on race and religion
sections.summary: Questions ask about efforts to build a civic engagement sector, sourcing and training facilitators, and tracking effects on social cohesion, plus addressing social media tensions and strengthening harmony.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what are the current efforts to build the civic engagement sector for skilled facilitators to lead conversations in the community on sensitive topics of race and religion; (b) how are suitable and effective facilitators sourced for, identified and trained; and (c) how will the tracking, evaluation and scaling of the positive effects of these conversations on social cohesion be made within the community.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) how does the Government intend to address tensions on racial insensitivities and discrimination on social media platforms; and (b) how does the Government intend to strengthen racial and religious harmony in Singapore.

sections.label: Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act
sections.summary: The MRHA, as amended in 2019, lets the Government respond more effectively to religious disharmony and strengthens safeguards against foreign influence threatening religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act (MRHA), as amended in 2019, allows the Government to respond more effectively to incidents of religious disharmony and strengthens our safeguards against foreign influence that threaten our religious harmony.

sections.label: Comments against Indians and Penal Code charge
sections.summary: Comments against Indians referencing a news article on foreign workers in dorms and COVID-19 infection rates led to charges under section 298A of the Penal Code for promoting enmity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This included comments against Indians whilst making reference to a news article on foreign workers living in dorms contributing to the apparent high COVID-19 infection rate in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: He was charged for offences of promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion or race under section 298A of the Penal Code.

sections.label: MCCY BRIDGE programme dialogues
sections.summary: MCCY's BRIDGE programme, launched in 2017, has to-date supported over 120 dialogues pertaining to race and religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MCCY's BRIDGE programme was launched in 2017 and has to-date supported over 120 such dialogues pertaining to race and religion.

sections.label: Teacher training for CCE conversations
sections.summary: Under the refreshed 2021 CCE curriculum, secondary and pre-university teachers will receive specialised training to facilitate conversations on contemporary issues including race and religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As part of the refreshed 2021 CCE curriculum, teachers in secondary schools and pre-university institutions will receive specialised training so that they can also facilitate conversations, discussions, dialogues on contemporary issues, including race and religion, to hone students' ability to understand different perspectives and engender a sense of empathy and respect for one another.
